Staying Cool Without Compromising Safety

British summers might not rival the Mediterranean, but when temperatures climb into the high twenties and thirties, a heavy textile touring jacket becomes unbearable. A dedicated summer jacket with mesh panels and ventilation lets the breeze flow through while maintaining crucial impact protection for those spirited B-road rides.

Mesh vs Vented Textile

Full mesh jackets use large panels of open-weave textile for maximum airflow but minimal weather protection. Vented textile jackets feature strategically placed zip-open vents on conventional construction, allowing you to open up in heat and close down when rain arrives. For UK touring where unexpected showers are always possible, vented textile is generally more practical.

Essential Features

  • CE armour — Never compromise on shoulder and elbow protection. Level 2 protectors are the minimum for touring speeds on any road.
  • Back protector pocket — Many summer jackets include a pocket but no protector. Budget for a separate CE Level 2 back protector.
  • Reflective panels — Summer evening rides mean lower sun angles and potential visibility issues. Reflective elements help.
  • Light colours — White, grey, and light blue reflect heat far better than black. Consider lighter colours for summer-specific gear.

Best Summer Touring Jackets

Rev It Torque 2 — Large mesh panels with sleek touring design. PWR mesh outer with SEESMART CE Level 2 armour at shoulders and elbows. Athletic fit without being restrictive.

Alpinestars Wake Air — Excellent airflow through chest and back panels. Removable waterproof liner handles light showers. Good value from a premium brand.

Oxford Arizona 1.0 — Budget pick with mesh panels, CE armour, and waterproof liner. Under a hundred pounds for remarkable touring value.

Klim Induction Pro — Maximum ventilation for the hottest days. Massive mesh panels front and back with characteristically robust Klim construction.

Even in a heatwave, never ride without proper armour. Road rash at 30mph is just as painful in July as it is in January. A good summer jacket keeps you cool and protected simultaneously.

Layering Strategy

Pair summer jackets with moisture-wicking base layers that pull sweat away from skin. Synthetic fabrics like polyester or merino wool work far better than cotton, which holds moisture and becomes clammy. A thin neck tube prevents sunburn on exposed skin above the collar.

Transitional Weather Strategy

British summers are unpredictable. A summer jacket with a packable waterproof liner gives you the best of both worlds. Keep the liner in a tank bag pocket so you can deploy it in seconds when the first drops fall. Some riders carry a lightweight waterproof shell that packs into a fist-sized pouch as emergency backup for their pure mesh jackets during unpredictable British touring weather. keyTakeaways: Vented textile jackets are more practical than full mesh in the UK because you can close them when showers hit.
Full mesh maximises airflow but offers minimal weather protection for sudden British rain.
Never drop below CE Level 2 shoulder and elbow armour, even in a heatwave.
Light colours reflect heat far better than black, a real benefit on hot days.
Carry a packable waterproof liner or shell so you are ready for unexpected showers.

pros: Keeps you cool and alert when temperatures climb into the high twenties.
Vented textile designs shut down quickly when a shower arrives.
Encourages riders to keep armour on rather than ride under-protected in heat.
cons: Full mesh offers little protection against rain or cold.
Many summer jackets omit the back protector, so you must buy one separately.

faq.q: Mesh or vented textile for UK summers?
faq.a: Vented textile is usually the better choice for British riding because you can zip the vents shut when an unexpected shower arrives, whereas full mesh offers almost no rain protection. Full mesh maximises airflow and suits genuinely hot, dry days, but the UK's changeable weather rewards a jacket you can seal up. Many vented jackets also include a packable waterproof liner for the best of both.

faq.q: Do summer jackets have enough armour?
faq.a: The good ones include CE Level 2 protectors at the shoulders and elbows, which you should never compromise on even in a heatwave, since road rash at 30mph hurts just as much in July. However, many summer jackets provide only a back protector pocket rather than the protector itself, so budget for a separate CE Level 2 back protector to complete the setup.

faq.q: What should I wear under a mesh jacket?
faq.a: Wear a moisture-wicking base layer in a synthetic fabric or merino wool to pull sweat away from your skin, as cotton holds moisture and turns clammy. A thin neck tube prevents sunburn on the exposed skin above your collar. On the hottest days some riders dampen the base layer before setting off, using the airflow through the mesh for evaporative cooling.

faq.q: How do I handle sudden rain in summer?
faq.a: Carry a packable waterproof liner or a lightweight shell that folds into a fist-sized pouch, and keep it in a tank bag pocket so you can deploy it in seconds. If your jacket has a removable waterproof liner, stow it where you can reach it quickly. British summers are unpredictable, and being caught in a downpour without cover quickly turns a warm ride cold and miserable.
